title: Obex takes first-loss exposure while requiring every funded project to grant legally enforceable recourse
content:
A.6.1.1.5.3.2.4 states: "Capital deployed through Obex carries explicit **first-loss** protection defined by the Incubator Prime. Each funded project must maintain **verifiable recourse** through token, equity, or revenue participation agreements enforceable by the Prime's legal wrapper."

The two halves are a deliberate trade. Taking the first-loss tranche means Obex absorbs initial losses before any other capital in a funded project is impaired — the most subordinated position available, and precisely what makes an incubator's money attractive to early teams and to co-investors sitting above it. In exchange, Obex demands claims that survive failure: equity, tokens, or revenue participation.

The word "enforceable" is where the Artifact's legal architecture becomes load-bearing rather than decorative. An on-chain Agent cannot sue anyone. Recourse against an early-stage company requires a legal person to hold the agreement and a court to enforce it, which is exactly why the three-layer Agent → Rubicon Foundation → Treadstone structure exists. The Foundation's mandate to "support the development, growth, and adoption of Obex" includes being the entity that can hold a contract.

The combination also has a specific risk signature that the transparency clause responds to. First-loss capital fails frequently and visibly by design, so A.6.1.1.5.3.2.5's requirement to publish **default rates** is not incidental — an incubator taking the first-loss tranche must disclose how often it loses, or its published yields are meaningless.
description: Capital carries explicit first-loss protection defined by the Incubator Prime, and each project must maintain verifiable recourse via token, equity or revenue participation agreements enforceable
